The request

I asked IT for an identity for my agent.
They said no.

No MFA, so it's a risk flag. Every request like it has been refused.
So my agent runs as me.

Your IT department isn't wrong to say no.

It's missing a way to say yes.

02 · Why IT is right

What our CISO sees

Credentials with no human

An app identity can't do MFA, so it's a risk flag

Agents with no owner

The builder leaves; the agent keeps running

Agents nobody can name

He can count thousands; he can't name them

MCP is a black box

Weak logging, untested restores. Policy: "no MCP"

A "no" without a mechanism just moves the risk

Personal access tokens, API keys in .env files, agents on laptops.
The traffic still happens, just where nobody can see it.

03 · A way to say yes

One front door

Agentown Entra identity, or on behalf of a user
Entra
token
AI gatewayAPI Management: validate token, allow-list, token limit, log
managed
identity
Models + toolsFoundry · MCP servers · Jira / GitHub (PAT held by the gateway)

Back doors closed: Foundry keys off, agents get no direct RBAC. Entra in, PAT out.

Whose permissions does it have?

on behalf of

It can do no more than the caller

Owner = the caller. The safer default. If the delegation isn't granted: refuse, or ask out of band.

agent as employee

It has its own rights

Now you need RBAC for who may ask it to do what. Prompt injection is risk #1: a ticket says "delete the hub".

The back door you already have

One token. It can comment and close.

Whoever holds it can do both, and GitHub records that you did it.

04 · Governance that holds

Three layers

1Org rulesetApplies to every agent: models, data zones, logging, owner required
2Agent contractPer agent, versioned: owner, identity, tools, data, budget
3RuntimeThe gateway stops it exceeding the contract, even when prompted to

"Draft a message" → "send a message" is a permission change, not a feature

Every change in authority gets a version, an approver and evidence.

From "no MCP" to a yes with conditions

before

"No MCP, please."

One approved exception. Everyone else waits, or goes round it.

after

"MCP only through the gateway."

With an owner, an identity, an allow-list and a log. The exception became the pattern.

Monday morning

  • List which apps can request tokens on behalf of your users
  • Close one PAT back door behind a gateway
  • Write a one-page contract for one agent

Your IT department isn't wrong to say no.
Give it a way to say yes.
